To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the decay of a vortex wake is strongly influenced by the ambient turbulence, (2) the ambient turbulence is strongly influenced by atmospheric conditions such as crosswind shear and proximity to the ground, and (3) these atmospheric conditions can significantly affect the persistence of a vortex wake.

the dissipation rate of a two-dimensional vortex pair is enhanced by the presence of a turbulent background and that this effect is increased when the vortex pair is subjected to crosswind shear or to the proximity of a surface.

the rate of decay and rolling moment induced on following aircraft by trailing vortex pairs increase with increasing background dissippation rate and crosswind shear, and decrease with increasing distance from the ground plane.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of neutral atmospheric turbulence on the decay of aircraft trailing vorts.
the effects of atmospheric turbulence and shear upon the dispersion of two-dimensional aircraft vortices.
the neutral atmospheric effects on vortex pair dispersion and decay, and the results are intended to serve as a basis for future work on the effects of the atmosphere upon vortex persistence.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the vortex wake hazard to aircraft following a large transport aircraft is significantly lessened by the effects of the neutral atmosphere, particularly the presence of a ground plane.
the neutral atmosphere has the effect of dispersing vortex pairs, thereby reducing the hazards associated with vortex encounters.
the neutral atmospheric effects on vortex wake dispersion and decay can be accurately modeled using the turbulent transport theory.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dissipation rate of the vortex pair is enhanced by the background turbulence, the crosswind shear and the ground plane.
the vortex wake hazard is significantly reduced in a neutral atmosphere.
vortex dissipation is enhanced in the presence of a mean shear, but that this effect is not large enough to offset the effect of increased dissipation due to the turbulent bath.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the vortex wake hazard is significantly reduced by a crosswind and the ground.

the persistence of trailing vortices in the atmosphere depends upon both the ambient turbulence and the atmospheric stability, and that the vortex wake is more persistent in stable atmospheric conditions.
vortex decay is strongly influenced by the atmospheric conditions.
